then.text: The Wrens ran the signals down here, round the clock: teleprinters, telephones, coded messages from the ships.
Admiral Ramsay's operations room is at the back. Go and see Mr Ellis there.
Halt! Who goes there? Password? No? Then you'll have to prove you're not a spy the old-fashioned way.
Ops room's at the back of the tunnel. Mind the step.

else.text: Restricted area. Unless you're with the guide, I'm afraid I can't let you any further.

then.text: There it is, back on the wall: the Channel, the beaches, the routes the ships took. Thank you.
You got past Joan? Then help me pin the map up. There. The beaches at Dunkirk, the three routes across, Y, X and Z, dodging the German guns and the sandbanks.
Ramsay worked in a room just like this with a handful of staff, almost without sleep, for nine days. They hoped to rescue 45,000 men. They brought back about 338,000.
Take the news to the Harbourmaster at the ferry terminal. He likes to hear it told.

else.text: The operations room. Admiral Ramsay's desk stood here. There's a map that wants putting back up, if Joan lets you through.

tunnel_medic.text: There was an underground hospital in these tunnels during the war, with an operating theatre. Wounded airmen and soldiers were brought straight in from the harbour.
Electric lights, generators and miles of passages. A whole little town in the chalk.
